utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. And good afternoon to you, Madam Registrar. If you could kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I only notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Thayer and Mr. Nicholls. We have been informed that there are some preliminaries. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone. A scheduling preliminary regarding next week, Mr. President. We have received the Chamber's order with respect to Witness -- the first witness who was on the list for Monday. We have been advised by that witness's attorney that he will be unavailable that day, and we are talking about Witness 119, to represent his client as authorised by the Chamber's order. The -- we have been in touch with the attorney. We are in a position to postpone the testimony at the court's pleasure, until later in the week. We had anticipated that for a number of potential reasons, Witness 119's testimony was tenuous in terms of it actually happening that day so we were already prepared to go ahead with the next two witnesses on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I feel a little bit confused. Is it 119 or 118?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I believe 119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. All right. Okay. Okay. All right. Okay. 119. Because the same -- he would be number 118 to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I got confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So we are prepared to proceed with the witnesses who are already scheduled to follow Witness 119. They will be arriving on Sunday. They will be proofed Sunday. They will be ready to go. We believe that we will be able to fill the day on Monday with those two witnesses' testimony. Their testimony may be completed on Monday. It's just as likely it will carry over to Tuesday. We always Witness number 4, our investigator, available to fill any gaps on Tuesday on the issue of the Drina Corps collection. In addition we are trying to see if Witness, I believe his number is 101, who is currently scheduled to testify next Friday, is available to come here earlier and to be ready to go Tuesday if there is an enormous gap that has emerged for some reason. The bottom line, Mr. President, is if the Court is so inclined we would like to postpone Witness 119's testimony until Friday next and we will do everything we can to fill any gaps that develop as a result of that movement, as I've just outlined for everyone. And again, it's the next two witnesses are PW-108, Witness number 166, and our 5th Engineering deputy commander, who we have given the provisional witness number of 188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long is the examination-in-chief of Witness 119 estimated?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's extremely difficult to estimate. We -- at this time, we have been given an indication that he is unwilling to be proofed. It could be anywhere from half an hour to two hours or two and a half hours. It just depends on how it unfolds. So we are -- I don't think it's going to be much longer than two hours, though, frankly, Your Honour. I can't see that realistically happening but it's possible, depending on his answers and his reluctance and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say, any of the Defence teams? Ms. Nikolic? There are two issues basically, the evidence, the testimony of 119 and the evidence of the others that would be -- will be anticipated according to Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to you and to my learned friends. As far as Witness 119 is concerned, this Defence has no objection. We are simply trying to meet the witness's requests. As for the rest of the schedule, I hear for the first time from my learned friend Mr. Thayer that the witness 108 could appear as early as Monday. I wasn't able to inform him that during today we received from the Commission for the Cooperation with The Hague Tribunal from Belgrade, upon Serbian government approval, certain material that could have to do with Witness 108. If there is a possibility, I'd kindly ask that we stick with the previous schedule, that is that Witness 108 be heard on Tuesday, so that I would be able to go through the material. It is in B/C/S and there are only two of us in the office who can deal with it. And then we would inform our esteemed colleagues as to what it has to do with. As for the other witnesses, Mr. Nikolic's Defence has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Again, likewise, Your Honour, we weren't aware of what my learned friend has just said. We would rather 101 remained in place towards the end of next week. That's our only representation. So far as 119 is concerned, we are neutral and have observed what the Trial Chamber has said in relation to the attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just two quick notes. My friends have been on notice or a little while that 108 would be available and scheduled to testify on Monday. I've sent out e-mails preparing them for that eventuality in case 119 went early. The problem we face, however, is we can -- I don't think there is a problem putting our 5th Engineering Battalion deputy commander in front of PW-108. The problem is I anticipate his testimony to be relatively brief so that would create a gap on Monday that I'm not sure we're not going to be in a position to fill. So although we are certainly willing to accommodate our friends in that regard and put 108 after the other witness, we would have a gap emerging on Monday if we were to delay 108 until Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think there are two things you need to address, both of you, both sides, and one is the emerging situation that calls for some practical solution, and the other is that if any of the Defence teams has a genuine problem, that also has to be addressed, and a solution found which -- be found that satisfies both of you. As at the moment, as at present, I think 108, do you have an estimate of the length of the duration of your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we are looking at about an hour on direct, and if I may add, one fall-back position we have frequently taken is put his direct testimony on on Monday, see how far we get and it will reduce the gap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You read my mind because this is precisely what I was trying to lead you to. Perhaps we could on Monday we could have the examination-in-chief only of this witness, and then proceed with the testimony of the other person, the second in line, if you ensure that that other person is also available, and then on Tuesday, depending on whether Ms. Nikolic would be ready or not, we could have either the cross-examination of 108 or the cross-examination of the other witness to be followed by the cross-examination of 108 which would be either late on Tuesday or on Wednesday. I mean those are my suggestions, if they are acceptable to both of you. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think it is acceptable and that we will inform as soon as possible the Chamber and the other side what it is that we need to be able to accept it on behalf of Nikolic's Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you'll try and work it out, Mr. Thayer. You'll try and work it out this way. There is another thing I need to discuss with my colleagues on this rescheduling. Incidentally, Judge Stole is still unwell and we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you work together along those lines and then if there are problems, Ms. Nikolic, we will do our best to ensure that everyone is -- everyone is given the appropriate opportunity to present his or her case. So is there any other preliminary you would wish to raise? Yes, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I announced this matter to my learned friends from the Prosecution as well. Yesterday's witness, in his testimony, particularly in its latter portion, went beyond the scope of the summaries we received as to the matter he was going to testify about according to 65 ter. Defence did not object and did not react until now because we thought it came from the witness himself without any prior intervention on the part of the Prosecutor. Today we are ready to go ahead with the cross-examination. We intend to conclude it. However, there was something that we wanted to inform the Bench about. In case that during cross-examination, there are some other new facts, like yesterday, we would kindly request that this witness be called back for additional cross-examination on such matters that may be new to this Defence. There was another matter as well. I believe that our colleagues from the Prosecution were also somewhat surprised by the development, and we as well as they, I believe, would not wish that this become a regular practice. This is why we did not object to the new facts which occurred beyond the scope of the -- of Rule 65 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Indeed, this information was 100 per cent new to, I think, all of us here. It did catch us very much by surprise, with respect to the reburial operation testimony. I think to be fair to our friends, if they can make an appropriate showing that his presence would be required for additional examination based on new information that emerges and we are ready for any new information that emerges from any other witness, then they should be given that opportunity upon the proper showing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've heard what you had to say and taking that into consideration, we'll provide accordingly, if the need for the return of Mr. Lazarevic arises in due course. Okay. And that applies to both of you actually. I mean both Prosecution and Defence. Anything else? In the meantime, can I have a revised estimate of the cross-examination, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. We will not cross-examine this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 minutes, Your Honour, depending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I expect to need less than 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. We will not examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We will stick to our estimate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which was?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I would have said about 20 minutes but having had a discussion with Ms. Nikolic, I anticipate she will cover a great deal of the ground that I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So good afternoon to you, Mr. Lazarevic. Welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're still testifying under oath and I want to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- remind you of the caution that I gave you at the beginning of yesterday's sitting, namely in relation to any questions that may be put to you which could potentially expose you to criminal proceedings. So Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, who, if anyone, you spoke to about your testimony before you came to The Hague to testify?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And since 1995, July of 1995, have you spoken with Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, yesterday at the end of your testimony, you indicated to the Prosecutor, on page 70 of yesterday's transcript, when he asked you question: And when do you recall first telling any investigator or anybody about this reburial operation and the people that were involved in it, and your role in it? Do you recall your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, no. Yesterday in this courtroom, Mr. Thayer asked you when was the first time you told any investigator or anybody about this so-called reburial operation. Do you recall that question from yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But no one before asked me about it or came to me to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct. You answered under oath here, "I did not. Nobody ever asked me as to what, when, why. Nobody ever asked me about that. If they had asked me, I would have told them." Do you recall that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could we get on e-court, please, 3D189, page 72 in B/C/S, page 114 in English. That's a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if my friends have a list of exhibits to use on cross-examination we would appreciate receiving that. If there is no list or if there are no documents to be used that's fine. But if there are, we would appreciate a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, this was -- this was placed in, in my understanding, under 65 ter number 3D189 by the Nikolic team. It's the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I don't think that's the spirit in which Mr. Thayer raised -- made his point. I think his point is it doesn't -- mind you, you using any document -- but you should give him prior notice of what documents you're going to use upon cross-examination. This is what he basically said. You haven't given him notice of any documents that you will be using in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's not a document. I can certainly try to go through this without showing the witness anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, you met with investigator Dean Manning, did you not, in November of 2002?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And at the very end of that interview, sir, Dean Manning, the investigator for the OTP, asked you specifically: "Q: In September and October of 1995, a number of these graves, including Branjevo, Kozluk and Orahovac, were opened up and the bodies removed, buried in secondary graves elsewhere. What do you know about that process?" Do you recall him asking you that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall your answer to Mr. Manning?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't answer anything. I didn't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, if I tell you that your answer to that specific question was: "I don't know anything about this and I did not take any part in that, apart from having heard stories about that in the company while I was still in my military duty. I heard that something of that sort, that the bodies were transferred, that the graves were moved, was going on, but I did not take any part in that." That was your first answer. Does that refresh your recollection, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably yes, now. Otherwise -- I mean earlier I couldn't remember that I answered anything to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: After that, Mr. Manning asked you: "Q. Who did they say had taken part in that?" Sir, do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, your answer to that specific question was: "No. Nobody ever gave me a definitive answer as to who was involved and who had done this. I myself was not a part of that and I have no knowledge of who was moving the graves and doing this sort of thing. During that period, I was in charge of performing other tasks. I was putting up some bridges on other locations with a group of people who were assigned to work with me on that." Do you remember telling Mr. Manning that, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that I said it, but I can't remember that I said anything or explained anything, and I can't recall giving those answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: If you had given that answer, that would have been a lie, wouldn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would, probably, but I can't remember giving answers to those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall when Mr. Manning asked you whether the Zvornik Brigade engineers were involved in the reburial of these people, of these graves?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he asked me? When who asked me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: He asked -- sir, Dean Manning, the investigator that you talked to in Banja Luka, you had one interview with that investigator, correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible that I said something, but I can't remember those questions from Banja Luka. I can't remember any questions about the reburial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, after Mr. Manning asked you what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are having a French lesson. Go ahead, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Does my learned friend have any objection to me allowing the witness to see the last few pages in B/C/S and having it in front of him?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any objection to that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Meek would like to thank you and he may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, sir, are you stating that you don't know whether you had an interview with Mr. Manning in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has already confirmed that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: At the top of page 72 there, you see where it starts, Mr. Manning asked you the question in September and October? Do you see that, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Following on down from that, probably towards the middle or the end of that page, you were asked about the Zvornik Brigade engineers being involved and your answer was, "I don't know whether anybody was there from our lot. I don't know." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as reburial is concerned, I don't know. But since it's in the document, I must have said it but I have no recollection of saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you'll just look back at the very top of that page, Mr. Manning asked you a question which encompassed the opening up and the bodies being removed, did he not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek -- yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. It's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Immediately after that, Mr. Planning was curious about what you had heard, if anything, about it, and you answered, "I was never in the -- in the circle of people where this subject, this issue, was discussed, either in the streets or in the unit or anywhere else." Do you recall giving that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, regarding the reburial, I must have heard from people and I probably gave that answer, but I can't recall now that we discussed it. Yes, it's true that he asked me questions but I don't remember answering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Has looking at that transcript refreshed your recollection that those questions were asked and that you did give those answers, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably did give those answers, but right now, just from this paper, I can't remember the statements I gave. But since it's all in the documents, it's probably right that I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And what you said wasn't true, was it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was true when he asked me that question, but I don't remember what I answered to those questions, but it's here in the document. It's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And since you have been in The Hague, you've had three sessions with the Prosecutor for proofing, have you not?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you listen to an audio copy of this interview or read it in your own language, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreter read it to me up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you confirmed that everything that you had said in this interview with Dean Manning in Banja Luka was true and correct, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's here in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall also when Dean Manning during the interview with you in Banja Luka told you, "No matter who listens to your responses, they will not believe you"?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Meek. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I am Jelena Nikolic, representing Drago Nikolic. I'd like to ask you some questions about the events in July 1995. You testified yesterday that you had a few days off in the month of July 1995, the last one being the 14th, and you used those days off to see your son off into the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It is a custom that is time-consuming, it's a tradition in our lands, people usually get a couple of days off for that family event?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's the custom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Other soldiers also were granted days off for such occasions?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depended on how easy it was at the specific time. Somebody would get two or three days off or a week even. Others couldn't get any.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the interpretation to catch up. Thank you. In July, when you were present at the three locations you testified about yesterday from the 15th to the 17th of July, at Orahovac, Kozluk, Branjevo, did you see, meet with or contact Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Not during the time of the burial. I never met him or heard from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But you know Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know him from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about the approximate time when the reburial happened because according to the material and documentation we received from the Office of the Prosecutor, one could say it could have been around mid-September 1995. Does that sound to you like the right time?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the exhumation and burial?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the month but it was not long after the first burial. I don't remember the dates. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From your evidence yesterday, I concluded that the lorries as well as the machinery that was engaged in the reburial, let's say in autumn 1995, did not belong to the Zvornik Brigade. Your equipment in the brigade was rather old and in poor state of repair.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the machines themselves, just the lorries that transported those machines, BGH-700 and 500.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you say not really, you mean to say that they did not belong to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not according to the establishment. They were requisitioned from other companies, enterprises, whereas the lorries that transported the machines, they belonged to enterprises that also provided the drivers. They were civilians. They were not uniformed personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you were giving evidence, I'd like to ask, can you confirm with certainty that Major Trbic was the person who coordinated the whole operation of reburial in autumn 1995? Was he also the officer who was responsible for all the activities related to exhumation?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you concluded that Captain Trbic was then your superior, as far as the operation was concerned, because you addressed him for anything you needed?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He also contacted me up there to see what was done and how it was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And in relation to all those activities, exhumation and coordination of meetings, you did not see Drago Nikolic for a single moment, for as long as it lasted?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not even when I occasionally went back to the base at the brigade. I just didn't run into him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Zvornik Brigade occasionally sent some of their troops as assistants to other areas that were covered by other corps, not the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Individual soldiers or units or even especially formed units were sent outside the area of activities of the brigade or the corps to help out elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't know. Some -- somebody may have been away on assignment, on orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you if I understood this correctly. I understood that only three members of your company were involved in the operation of exhumation in autumn 1995.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from our unit? Two machine operators and the driver who transported the machines on the lorry. He would bring the machines and then go away.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you personally were aware only of those three locations?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three locations, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And at that time, you did not know where the bodies would be reburied?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you were not shown a map or an order indicating locations from which bodies were to be taken away and other locations to which they were supposed to be taken?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew the locations where they were buried the first time, but where they were taken to be reburied, I didn't know, and I don't know to date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you say, "I know," you mean those three locations you testified about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But you didn't see a map or an order indicating that bodies would be reburied elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see a map and nobody told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily a map. A document.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From all this, one is prone to conclude that details of the operation were known only to a small number of persons who were directly involved.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's probable that other army personnel also knew about it, but there were only a few of us, a group of soldiers, who were designated to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the process of exhumation was mostly by night.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When it was already dark.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, it didn't take long.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. Five, six days maybe, six days max.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From the material disclosed to us by the Office of the Prosecutor, one could conclude that it lasted for three consecutive nights. Would you say that was right?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I think it took longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure it wasn't three nights because at Branjevo, it's a long way, and it took longer. I believe we stayed down there for two nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that in a way, this was a secret operation, judging by the way how it was carried out and how long it took?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the few of us who were involved were certainly aware of it, but a broader circle of soldiers and civilians could also have been aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But you don't know many details really about what was going on and why?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Just a correction to the interpretation of my question. My question was: In reality, very few persons were really aware of the details. I believe the witness understood me properly but it was not properly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, did you hear what Ms. Nikolic said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what is your version of -- what was your answer? Her question was in reality it was suggested to you that in reality very few persons were really aware of the details. Would you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish me to amplify it further, Ms. Nikolic, or are you satisfied with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour. I would like to thank you Mr. Lazarevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you, Madam Nikolic. Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that you understand, I'm going to ask you a few questions on behalf of Vinko Pandurevic, who, in 1995, was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. I dare say you remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the commander, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I want to ask you first of all a few questions about vehicle work logs, and I dare say you saw a lot of those in 1995, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we agree that each vehicle work log covers a period of a month, starting with the first day of the month and ending with the last day of the month?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way logs are issued, for a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the log is in two parts. The first part records the fact that a vehicle has been provided with fuel, and the second part records the use of the vehicle. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The first part is signed by the fuel pump attendant at the time that the vehicle is fueled; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the second part, as we'll see in a minute, could be filled in by virtually anybody, sometime before the end of the month; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day it must be recorded where the vehicle went, the route. It must be signed by the commander, maybe some sort of officer. Somebody has to sign for the use of the vehicle for that day, so that the use of the -- the consumption of fuel can be justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've saved me a few questions there. It follows, therefore, doesn't it, that a vehicle work log is only opened or created when a vehicle is given fuel?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A log is issued every first of the month, and it is filled in date by date, as the vehicle was used, so that the operator or the driver would have justification for his consumption of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to try and illustrate the point I'm making you by slowing again a document that Mr. Thayer showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if we could put into e-court please, P302.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it helps the witness and my friend I have the original. We had some legibility issues. I can have it handed to the witness for his convenience.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's very kind indeed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you saw this document yesterday, Mr. Lazarevic, so you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'll just confirm, won't you, that this is not a vehicle that belonged to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if needed, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you'll confirm also, will you, that Kovacevic, Veljko, was not a member of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not even work at the Glinica Factory with that piece of machinery but once it is requisitioned, he was supposed to operate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I don't think you've answered my question. He wasn't a member of the Zvornik Brigade, was he?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only after the machine had been requisitioned. Then he would be made part of the company or the brigade. He was employed elsewhere and occasionally he would come with his machinery to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the point I was trying to make earlier is that document would have been created on the 15th of July when this vehicle, which belonged to another company, arrived to take fuel, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go over the page, please? Over the page there are two entries relating to the use of this vehicle, on the 15th and the 17th of July. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And both of those entries have been written and signed by the same person, haven't they?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And does it appear to you they have been written in the same pen?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it's the same pen, but the signature is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And looking at the signature, whatever it does say, it certainly doesn't say Kovacevic, Veljko, does it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it belongs to someone from our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. Again, I want you to look at another document you saw yesterday. Can we have a look, please, at P301? And this one of course is the one that's in e-court backwards so can we have a look at the fueling page which would be the second page on this document? Thank you. I'm sorry, I didn't look, but has the witness got the original of this document? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: He does, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Lazarevic, not a vehicle that belonged to the Zvornik Brigade, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But it drew fuel on a few days during the month of July?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And a Rovokopac Torpedo is a small tractor-like vehicle similar to the one which you described as being of no use at Kozluk. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we go to the page that deals with the use of the vehicle, which is the first page in e-court? And you simply have to turn the document over, Mr. Lazarevic. Again, all the entries and all the signatures in the same handwriting; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see from those entries, as you established in some detail with Mr. Thayer yesterday, that this vehicle is said to have been at Orahovac on the 14th of July; do you agree with that, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not at Orahovac on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I appreciate you say that, but the document says it was, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it in the document, but at Orahovac on the 14th, there was a larger machine. It was a BGH-500 that I saw there, not this one. I don't know who inserted this data.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in fact, would you go further as to say such a vehicle would have been no use at Orahovac, from what you saw of the work required there?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, forgive me, you've used the date the 14th, but as I understand your evidence, you were at Orahovac on the 15th of July, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there on the 14th -- on the 15th, but on the 14th the machine had been sent to Orahovac, and on the 15th, I found it there; not this machine, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, can we now go to P297? And we'll need in e-court page 134 in the B/C/S, page 14 in the English, and if Mr. Thayer would be so kind to provide the witness with the original, he will need to look at page 125.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I hope you're reading the daily orders book for the Engineering Company for the date of the 14th of July of 1995. Am I correct in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you confirm that on the 14th of July, there were no orders from the Zvornik Brigade for vehicles to go to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no mention or, rather, the order doesn't say which machine was up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, no, it says more than that. There are no orders for vehicles to go to Orahovac at all on the 14th of July, are there?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th, I was at home. I wasn't at the unit that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to get into unnecessary difficulty with you, Mr. Lazarevic. I'm simply asking you to confirm what the orders say for that day, whether you were at home or not. You've been asked to look at a lot of these orders and read them and state what they say. I'm asking you simply to agree that on the 14th of July, there were no orders from the Zvornik Brigade Engineering Company for vehicles to go to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find any such a thing in this text. I don't see any vehicles being mentioned going up there. It is only mentioned that the officer on duty at the company on the 14th of July will be Vojislav Sekonjic, who was the company officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we conclude that if there were any vehicles at Orahovac on the 14th of July, they were sent there by somebody others than the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a vehicle -- there were vehicles on the 14th. That has been proven. There was a machine from our brigade that had been sent up there, and I found it there on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just a few more questions on this. In summary, therefore, a vehicle work log is merely an indicator that a vehicle has been given fuel by the Zvornik Brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's not an indication that that vehicle has been mobilised by the Zvornik Brigade or is under the control or direction of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that particular vehicle had a work order opened for, then it had been mobilised by the Zvornik Brigade for the time necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, that's what I thought you just disagreed with. I thought you just agreed with the idea that all a vehicle work log is is an indication that a vehicle has received fuel and nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was very clear. The answer was very clear. And I think we are getting argumentative with this witness if betake it further. He's asked the question and received the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Lines 8 to 11, page 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are unanimously of the opinion that what the witness previously stated might call for some clarification, so go ahead, Mr. Haynes. And witness, Mr. Lazarevic, if you wish Mr. Haynes to put the question again to you, we'll do that. Otherwise, if you remember it you may proceed to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, do you know what arrangements there were between the Zvornik Brigade and, for example, the civil protection authorities concerning the provision of fuel to vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. It was not up to me to take care of that. The brigade cooperated with them, whenever it found it necessary. I don't know what sort of a mechanism was in place. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- again, if you don't know the answer to this, then say so, but I'll ask you the question. Do you know whether there was any accounting procedure between the civil protection authorities and the brigade concerning the provision of fuel to vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, between the brigade and the civil protection authorities, well, we always fueled our tanks at the gas station. As for the rest ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But there was cooperation between the brigade and the civil protection authorities concerning the provision of fuel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you stand by your original answer, do you, that a vehicle work log is merely an indication that a vehicle has been provided with fuel by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Asked and answered, Your Honour, but the witness has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the civil protection authorities were responsible for sanitation and hygiene; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess so. We know what civil protection is for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in wartime that included the burying of dead bodies, unfortunately, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we are of course aware that in July of 1995, the weather was very hot and the bodies you saw were decomposing very quickly, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And doubtless, even you'd agree that they presented a health risk to the general public?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At Orahovac, it was your impression that the burial work was being conducted by members of the civil protection authorities; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were there working on it, with the assistance of the machine -- machines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And your function was merely to be on hand in case of mechanical problems, as I understand your evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And although you left before the job was finished, your information was that the job was finished. In other words, that every body was buried?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And according to what you know, there is no possibility of a number of dead bodies being visible in the field at Orahovac, say, two or three days later?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been, but I didn't go there to check, after they finished. After they had finished that, I didn't go up there any more. It is possible that they didn't perform their task all too well, that they didn't cover all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you went to Kozluk, did you take with you any sort of radio or communication device?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. I never had such a thing in my possession, throughout the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What about the soldiers you saw there with the painted faces? Did any of them appear to have radio communications devices?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even approach them. They were a bit further away. I don't know what they were doing up there. I just saw them standing there in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But whoever it was who arranged for a bigger machine to arrive at Kozluk, it had nothing to do with you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First a small machine arrived with Milos Mitrovic. It wasn't able to do much. And then later a larger machine followed. I suppose that up there at the unit, they realised that he wasn't able to do anything with the small machine and then they sent a larger one, a ULT 220.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Whilst we are on the subject of ULT 220s, during the course of the burials that you witnessed, you saw two ULT 220s, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other one came occasionally, the aluminum oxide factory was relatively nearby and it came when necessary. However, there was only one ULT there most of the time, not two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I didn't mean that you saw them at the same time, but you saw a second ULT, which belonged to a quarry in Branjevo; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branjevo, yes, that machine belonged to the quarry. As for the aluminum oxide factory, which came occasionally, well, I don't know where it was the rest of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The ULT that belonged to the quarry was driven by a man called Boskovic, Rade, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And, again, he was not a member of the Zvornik Brigade, was he?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally, when the machine was there, he was there with it so he must have been a member at such times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we come to the reburials operation? When you said yesterday it was carried out by the same persons, do you mean that the drivers were again Kovacevic, Veljko, and Boskovic, Rade?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not Veljko, just Rade Boskovic, and Cvijetin Ristanovic as well as Miladinovic, I think his first name is Milovan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Boskovic did not take any part in the reburial or the transfer. That machine was not present, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, the organisation, which seemed to you to be principally responsible for the reburial, was the civil protection authority; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've withheld objections on some very similar questions that I believe misstate the prior testimony of this witness on this very point. I think he was very clear in his answers as to who he considered responsible based on his experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I've never seen it as a function of cross-examination to accept everything a witness says according to the interpretation of the Prosecutor and stay faithful to that. I'm entitled to put suggestions to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but also juxtaposed to what he's stated in his evidence, which I shouldn't repeat in his presence, but which you are aware of. In relation to the reburials he was very specific as to who was giving orders and to whom they were reporting, and I think if you wish to clarify that with the witness, you need to remind him of that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I will come on to that, yes. I have no difficulty with that, but I'm really dealing with the physical mechanics of it. That's the question I'm putting to him, who did it seem to him was responsible for manning and operating and organising the machines and I'm suggesting that he said it was the same people, the civil protection authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I think the prior testimony is clear as to who this witness previously testified was involved in this reburial operation based on his experience and his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, apart from what you have already told us, who did it seem to you was responsible for providing the human and mechanical and organisational resources, particularly in relation to the machines? Was it the civil protection authority or was it someone else? Are you happy with the way I phrased it, Mr. Haynes or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The civil protection authority could only ask the companies to lend them machines. As for the army, they can requisition machines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's any clearer but I'm going to leave it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may have overheard because I had my microphone on. I said I wouldn't dare intervene again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to see if I can help you with the date on which these operations took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I wonder if we could have in e-court please P2103 at page 240.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you see that, Mr. Lazarevic? Now, let me explain these photographs to you. We accept, all of us in this case, that these photographs are evidence of the fact that the reburials at Orahovac took place sometime between the first photograph on the 7th of September and the second photograph on the 27th of September. And Orahovac was one of the places you went to, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Seeing those photographs, and as it were, the dates between which the state of the earth was altered, do you now accept that when you played whatever part it was you played in the reburial operation, it was sometime in the middle of September?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was designated by my command. I was to be the one from the Engineering Company to be there with the men who were doing it, in the same way I was present at the first burial, when I was designated to be there, and that's how they appointed me the second time as well. Major Jokic, Slavko Bogicevic and the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, how much further?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm so close to finishing, I'd crave your indulgence and, well, not so much yours but those who need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it okay? We may be here a few more minutes and then we'll have the usual break.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you also aware in September of 1995, that there was heavy fighting going on in the Krajina region?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Krajina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And were you aware that members of the Zvornik Brigade took part in that fighting? Perhaps even members of your own unit?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sent there too at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you aware that the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko Pandurevic, commanded a unit in Krajina for a period in September?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And were you aware that he was away from the command of the Zvornik Brigade until about the 27th of September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they stayed behind after we left. I don't know the date when they returned to the command. But I know the commander was there, around, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You mean in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you know also, don't you, that in the absence of Commander Pandurevic, his deputy was Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he as Chief of Staff had that responsibility, among others, to stand in for the commander when he was away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And amongst his other responsibilities was direct responsibility for the Engineering Company, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, you told us a lot yesterday about the chain of command in the Engineering Company, but Dragan Jokic answered to Dragan Obrenovic, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Then -- do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I do, Mr. President, it will be brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just have a few questions for you this afternoon. Can you recall in any more detail the type of truck that was used to transport the bodies away from these reburial sites where you were present?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were Shtier [phoen] trucks. They were owned by a hauling company, Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just describe what these trucks look like, what their general design is, how do they function?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large heavy-duty truck, for instance kippers [phoen], tri-axles, trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mean three axles, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on the back of these trucks, is there a bed or some kind of container?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do these trucks tip in the back?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, the chassis, there are two sides to it. When it tips, the one side opens automatically when you unload.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall the capacity of these trucks, in terms of the payload in the back in cubic metres or however you would measure the capacity that these loads or that these trucks can carry in the back?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think its carrying capacity was 12 cubic metres, as designated, but when you really need to fill it, you can even put 16, but normal capacity is 12 cubic metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you testified a little while ago in answer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. That's how it would have come out of the factory. What's more important is whether it had -- any alterations had been done to the truck to extend its cubic metre capacity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes what? Was it left in the same condition as it was when it came out of the factory? That is, with a capacity of 12 cubic metres? Or was that capacity increased?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In practice, and that's the case with all those hauling companies, they would increase the height of the chassis to increase the possible payload. So the sides were built on by the enterprise so they were increased by 20, 30 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I asked the question because that is what is normally done in my country, too, so I anticipated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned in answer to a question from my friend Ms. Nikolic that you recall that it took two nights to complete the exhumations of Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the order in which these burial sites that you've told us about were exhumed? Do you remember which came first, second and then last?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First one was Orahovac. The second was Kozluk, the gravel site. And the third one was the farm in Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when the bodies were finally exhumed and then transported away from Branjevo after that second night, where did the BGH and the ULT go?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first night, when we were still working, it stayed at the farm. And then we came back the second night to finish. They were not driven back. They stayed there on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then on the second night, when the exhumations were completed at Branjevo, where did the BGH and the ULT go?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were taken back to base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And by "base," do you mean your Engineering Company command at the youth settlement?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you just stated that on the first night, these vehicles stayed there on the road, which road are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close to the site, where the barns are.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not far from the barns.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter number 1801 on e-court, please? And with Madam Usher's assistance, I would like to hand a hard copy, because I think it will be a little easier for the witness to look at up close. It doesn't need to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us yesterday that you do not read English. Sir, it is the Prosecution's contention that this aerial photograph depicts an area to the left where new exhumation or excavation has occurred, that area being in the general area you indicated yesterday that the initial burials occurred. And it is further the Prosecution's contention that a backhoe and an excavator or a backhoe/excavator and a front loader are present as well in this photograph, near to the pigsties or stable area. This imagery has been represented by the US government to have been taken on or about the 27th of September 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment before you answer, Mr. Lazarevic. Yes, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe my learned friend is completely beyond the scope of cross-examination, as far as Branjevo is concerned, and the questions I asked in relation to that. I believe this is a repetition of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't heard the question as yet. What he's been asked for the time being is almost nothing. So yes, Mr. Meek? I'll of course will take a decision on your submission is correct or not once we've heard the question. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would join in Ms. Nikolic's objection and also point out that this is a leading and suggestive question. We don't need to hear the end of it to know that it is. It's redirect and he doesn't have the right to ask leading, suggestive questions like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'd support that. Any question that contains the phrase, "It is further the Prosecution's contention," is opinionated and leading and is not permissible either in direct examination or re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May I respond, Mr. President, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: First, Mr. President, I'm not posing this question, which has yet to come in response to a question from my friend Ms. Nikolic. I am responding to a series of questions from Mr. Haynes in which he asked this witness some specific questions regarding certain dates of activity. It is for that purpose that I'm going to ask this witness the question I intend to ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please come to your question, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we have been advised by the US government that this photograph was taken on 27 September 1995. Does that help your memory at all as to whether your participation in these exhumations occurred in the beginning of September, the middle of September, or the end of September?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At this stage, before he answers, I need to confirm with my colleagues that the question can be answered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Lazarevic, if you could answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is again the location at Branjevo, at the grave that I marked several times on the screen. This second square here in the second part is probably where the machinery was. If I understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His question, I don't think you did understand Mr. Thayer's question. You either repeat your question, Mr. Thayer, or I do it, one of the two. I think you should repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you just identified both the area in which you have previously identified the burials taking place. First of all, can you confirm that that area is the area in which the exhumations also took place? And I'd ask to you look at your screen because perhaps it will be a good time to make some markings, with Madam Usher's assistance. Can you mark the area in which the exhumations occurred?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you testified just a few moments ago that the machines were parked on a road near the stables. Can you just place an X in the area you recall those machines being parked, sir, during the course of the exhumations?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, at the junction of this road that goes towards Lokanj. I think that's the section, as far as I remember [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you could just turn that into an X, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Should I --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think that will do. Now, again, my question is: We have been told by the US government this photograph was taken on 27th of September 1995. Having made the markings you just made and based on your recollection, does this image help you recall whether these exhumations took place in the beginning of the month, the middle of the month, or at the end of the month?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact date. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Thank you. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You need to sign in the lower right-hand corner and today's date, which is the 30th.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it the 30th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 30th, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, that brings to an end your testimony. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over and last but not least I wish you a safe journey back home on behalf of everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now we can proceed with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have distributed the tender list. I trust everybody has a copy. We just have one additional exhibit, that being the one just -- or two additional exhibits, that being the unmarked version of this aerial photograph, 1801, and the second is the same exhibit as marked by the witness, that is PIC 00144.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections? They are so admitted. Any of the Defence teams, I don't think so -- yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would like to admit only a portion of the interview this witness gave Dean Manning, and again it's been listed in e-court as 3D189. In the English version, only page 114, the ERN number would be L0085810 through 81 or 512. I'm sorry, 812, three pages. And there is only one page in the B/C/S, Your Honour, that corresponds, and that would be page 72 or the ERN numbers T0004501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meek. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection from any of the other Defence teams? None. So admitted. Any --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, on the page I'm looking at, the B/C/S, I just looked at the transcript, it looks to me like it is 45011. Which I don't know why there is five digits on the end of that but -- it's page 72 of 72 of the B/C/S, one page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you but I also find it strange that it has five digits after the first three zeros. I don't know. Perhaps you can check it together with Mr. Thayer and with the registrar and then if it's not the correct entry, we can change it in due course. All right? Okay. That settles Mr. Lazarevic. Next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Just before the witness is brought in, I think that an advising the witness of his rights under Rule 90(E) is appropriate. I've explained the rule to him and that that he may be given that caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are no protective measures in place?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You are about to start giving evidence. The first thing we have to do before you proceed is for you to make the solemn declaration that is required under our rules, that you will be testifying the truth and the whole truth. Madam Usher is going to hand you the text. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivanovic. Please make yourself comfortable. Take a seat. Again, before we proceed, please listen carefully to what I'm going to tell you now. In the course of your testimony, since you are one of the persons that lived through the events that the Prosecution is alleging to have happened in July of 1995, and you were a soldier on active duty at the time, there may be questions put to you that, if you answer truthfully, could possibly expose you to criminal proceedings. I'm not saying that such questions will be asked but they may be asked. I don't know what your story is. In case such questions are put to you, you have a right to ask the Trial Chamber to exempt you from answering such questions. We will hear you. We will hear what you have to say. And then we can decide either to grant you such an exemption or to compel you to answer the questions notwithstanding that they could potentially expose you to criminal proceedings. If we do compel you to answer such questions, you have a further right under our rules, namely that unless what you state here in answering those questions is false testimony, then whatever you state will not and cannot be used against you in any further or future proceedings that could be taken against you. So you are covered on that as well. Have you understood what I have just explained to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.
